# User guide: The share guard

## In plain words

Some commands read a whole folder tree. If such a command runs over your Unraid shares or over a network mount, it can make the whole server stop answering. The share guard stops these commands before they start. The agent gets a short reason and the path to use instead, and it normally tries again at once on the right path. The guard has six protections. Each protection is a separate setting. You set a default for the whole server, and you can set a different value for one workspace. You can lock a workspace down, or you can leave it fully open. You see each refusal in the Activity tray.

## Where to find it

- **Settings, Configuration** tab, card **General**, part **Advanced**: the master setting **Guard the share filesystem (recommended)**, and below it one setting for each protection.
- **The row menu of a workspace** (the three-dot icon on a row in the drawer): the item **Protection settings…**.
- **Activity tray**: shows each refused command and each change that you make to the protections of a workspace.

Words used on this page:

- **Recursive read**: a command that goes into every folder below a start folder. Examples are `find`, `grep -r`, `du`, `ls -R` and `git status` over a large tree.
- **Share filesystem**: the Unraid layer that joins your disks under `/mnt/user`. Heavy reading over it can freeze the whole server.
- **Pool path**: the real folder of a share on its pool, for example `/mnt/cache/appdata`. Reading there does not use the share filesystem, so it is safe.
- **Network mount**: a folder that comes from another machine, for example under `/mnt/remotes`.
- **Helper workspace**: a workspace that an agent started. **Top-level workspace**: a workspace that you started.
- **Hidden share view**: a private view of the disk in which the shares and the network mounts are empty. Only the folder of the workspace and the paths that its task names are put back.

## The protections

| Protection | What it does when it is On | Server default |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Shell guard** | The shell of the workspace refuses recursive reads over shares and network mounts. | On |
| **Agent tool guard** | The tools of the agent refuse the same reads. Claude Code, OpenCode and OpenCode 2 have this protection. | On |
| **Hidden share view** | The workspace sees no shares and no network mounts, except the paths that it needs. | On for helper workspaces, Off for top-level workspaces |
| **Hide ssh keys** | The hidden view has no ssh keys, so the agent cannot ssh to this server or to another host. Applies only when the hidden view is On. | On |
| **Docker mount check** | The `docker` command refuses a mount of a share, `/` or `/mnt`. Applies only when the hidden view is On. | On |
| **Drop admin powers** | The hidden view drops the admin powers that could undo it, and blocks new privileges. Applies only when the hidden view is On. | On |

The master setting **Guard the share filesystem (recommended)** comes first. When it is Off, every protection is off for every workspace, whatever the other settings say.

The value of a protection for one workspace is its own choice, or else the server default. The plugin fixes the value when the workspace starts.

## How to use it

### What is refused

The shell guard and the agent tool guard refuse a recursive command in these cases:

- The start folder is under `/mnt/user`, `/mnt/user0`, `/mnt/remotes` or another network mount.
- The command starts at `/` or at `/mnt` and does not stay on one file system.

They allow a command that reads one named file, a command that goes only one level deep, and any command over a pool path. A refusal tells the agent the pool path for the share when the share lives on one pool only. For a share on the array, it tells the agent to name a smaller folder.

### Set the server defaults

1. Open **Settings**, then the **Configuration** tab, then the card **General**.
2. Select **Advanced** to open it.
3. Find **Guard the share filesystem (recommended)**. Choose **On (recommended)** or **Off**.
4. Below it, find the setting of each protection and choose **On** or **Off**. The two rows **Hidden share view for helper workspaces** and **Hidden share view for top-level workspaces** set the default of the hidden view for each kind of workspace.
5. Expect: each change saves at once. A workspace that is already running keeps its old protections until you start it again.

An agent cannot change these settings.

### Set the protections of one workspace

1. In the drawer, open the three-dot menu of the workspace.
2. Choose **Protection settings…**. A dialog opens with one row for each protection.
3. For each row, choose **Use the server default (On)** or **Use the server default (Off)**, **On** or **Off**. The first choice shows the value that the server default has now.
4. Choose **Save**. When you turned a protection **Off**, the plugin asks first. It asks because a wrong command can freeze the server.
5. Expect: a short message says that the change applies from the next start of the workspace. The Activity tray shows one record for each protection that you changed. Close and start the workspace again to use it.

The dialog says when the master setting is Off. Then every protection is off, whatever you choose in the dialog.

Only you can set this. An agent cannot set it with a tool, and a script cannot set it with the command `admin-agent`.

### Examples

- **Fully open workspace.** You want one helper to do everything its parent can do. Open **Protection settings…** and set **Shell guard**, **Agent tool guard** and **Hidden share view** to **Off**. The three other protections apply only to the hidden view, so they do nothing then.
- **Fully locked workspace.** You want a top-level workspace that cannot read the shares. Set **Shell guard**, **Agent tool guard**, **Hidden share view**, **Hide ssh keys**, **Docker mount check** and **Drop admin powers** to **On**.
- **A helper that may use docker freely.** Leave the hidden view On. Set **Docker mount check** to **Off**.
- **All helpers see the whole disk.** On the Settings page, set **Hidden share view for helper workspaces** to **Off**.

### See what the guard refused

Open the **Activity tray**. Each refusal shows the workspace, the agent and the command, cut to 200 characters. The tray shows at most one row for each workspace in each minute. A second refusal inside the same minute is still refused, and it is only not shown again. The plugin log has a line for each refusal that the hook makes.

## Settings

| Setting | Where | Default | Effect |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Guard the share filesystem (recommended)** | Settings, Configuration, General, Advanced | On (recommended) | Off turns off every protection for every workspace. |
| **Shell guard** | The same part | On | Off turns off the shell wrapper for workspaces that have no own choice. |
| **Agent tool guard** | The same part | On | Off turns off the agent hooks for workspaces that have no own choice. |
| **Hidden share view for helper workspaces** | The same part | On | Off lets helpers see the shares. |
| **Hidden share view for top-level workspaces** | The same part | Off | On hides the shares from top-level workspaces. |
| **Hide ssh keys** | The same part | On | Off keeps the ssh keys visible in the hidden view. |
| **Docker mount check** | The same part | On | Off lets `docker` mount any path in the hidden view. |
| **Drop admin powers** | The same part | On | Off keeps the admin powers in the hidden view. |
| **Protection settings…** | The row menu of a workspace | Each row: use the server default | Each row can be On or Off for that workspace, from its next start. |

## What to do when something looks wrong

| What you see | Likely cause | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| An agent says "aicli guard: refused" and names a pool path. | The agent ran a recursive command over a share. | Nothing. The agent should repeat the command on the pool path. If it does not, tell it to use that path. |
| An agent says "refused" and asks for a smaller folder. | The share is on the array, or the folder is a network mount, so no pool path exists. | Tell the agent which folder to search. Or set **Shell guard** and **Agent tool guard** to Off for that workspace, if you accept the risk. |
| You changed a protection, but a command is still refused or still allowed. | The workspace has not started again since you changed it. | Close the workspace and start it again. |
| You turned the master setting off, but an agent still has a protection. | The workspace is old and keeps its shell. | Start the workspace again. |
| A helper cannot find a folder that its parent can see. | The hidden share view is On, and the task did not name the folder. | Name the folder in the task, or set **Hidden share view** to Off for that workspace. |
